title: Nodal-Line Semimetals with Non-Quantized Berry Phase
authors: Zhi-Xia Li, Liangliang Huang, Min-Xue Yang, Feng Tang, D. Y. Xing, Wei Chen
abstract: Nodal-line semimetals (NLSMs) are topological materials characterized by one-dimensional band crossings in momentum space, which typically carry a Berry phase quantized to integer multiples of $π$. Here, we extend the conventional paradigm to a class of NLSMs in which the Berry phase can take arbitrary fractional or even irrational multiples of $π$. This non-quantized Berry phase leads to a splitting of Landau levels when a magnetic field is applied parallel to the nodal ring, an effect that can be detected via Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations in the magnetoconductivity. Despite the absence of a quantized topological invariant, drumhead-like surface states with weak dispersion persist at open boundaries. Notably, two identical surface states localize on the same boundary, in contrast to conventional NLSMs, where they reside on opposite boundaries. A systematic symmetry analysis shows that such NLSMs can be realized in a broad range of magnetic space groups. Our work opens a new avenue for exploring NLSMs beyond the conventional framework of a quantized Berry phase.
summary: This work explores Nodal-Line Semimetals where the topological Berry phase is not restricted to quantized values. By analyzing the consequences of a non-quantized Berry phase, the authors predict unique signatures in Landau level quantization and surface state formation. The findings open a new theoretical avenue for characterizing topological materials beyond conventional quantized topological invariants.
main_problem: The paper extends the study of Nodal-Line Semimetals (NLSMs) to a class where the Berry phase is non-quantized, moving beyond the conventional framework of integer multiples of $\pi$. It investigates the physical consequences of this non-quantization.
main_result: The non-quantized Berry phase causes a splitting of Landau levels when a magnetic field is applied parallel to the nodal ring, an effect detectable via Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations. Furthermore, it predicts the existence of two identical surface states localizing on the same boundary.
method: The study combines theoretical calculations (e.g., solving Landau Level problems, symmetry analysis) with the analysis of experimental signatures derived from quantum oscillations ($\delta\sigma_{yy}$).
model_or_system: The system is a class of NLSMs characterized by one-dimensional band crossings in momentum space, modeled using a specific three-band Hamiltonian. The analysis considers the effect of a magnetic field applied parallel to the nodal ring.
key_observables: Berry phase ($\phi_B$), Landau Level (LL) splitting, Shubnikov-de Haas (SdH) oscillations in magnetoconductivity ($\delta\sigma_{yy}$), and surface state spectral weight ($W$).
important_parameters: The Berry phase ($\phi_B$) is the key parameter, which can take arbitrary fractional or irrational multiples of $\pi$. The magnetic field ($B$) and Fermi energy ($E_F$) are also crucial.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a specific three-band model Hamiltonian and utilizes asymptotic analysis for quantum oscillation fitting.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the band structure with nodal rings and cross-sections ($\alpha_1-\alpha_4$), plot Landau Levels versus $\phi_B$, and show the nonlinear fitting of $\delta\sigma_{yy}$ data to extract phase shifts.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the non-quantized Berry phase, analyzes the resulting LL splitting via theoretical calculations, and then confirms this prediction by fitting the characteristic frequency and phase shifts observed in magnetoconductivity measurements.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter theory, the study of topological invariants and their breakdown (non-quantized phases) touches upon concepts of topological order and robustness, which are relevant to understanding exotic quantum states in engineered systems.
